# Logging

The logging interface is the same for every logging service of Grow Codes. The __DISPLAY__ client
gives you a `LogClient` for sending (a batching client on top of the __DISPLAY__ exporter) and, when
the service has a query API, a `LogQueryClient` for searching (see [Functions](functions.md) for
the accessors and the service options such as streams, indexes or labels). The examples call
them `logs` and `query`.

## Records

| Field | Type | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| `timestamp` | time | defaults to now |
| `severity` | `Severity` | OpenTelemetry numbers: `Trace=1`, `Debug=5`, `Info=9`, `Warn=13`, `Error=17`, `Fatal=21` |
| `severityText` | string | `TRACE` … `FATAL` or the vendor's text |
| `body` | string | the message; structured bodies are JSON-encoded |
| `attributes` | map | string, number, boolean, lists and nested maps |
| `resource` | map | `service.name`, `service.version`, `deployment.environment`, `host.name` |
| `traceId` / `spanId` / `traceFlags` | hex / int | filled from the active OpenTelemetry span when missing |

## Send logs

`send` and `sendBatch` only **enqueue**: a background worker batches records and exports them.
Each record passes the `RedactionProcessor` first. Call `flush()` when you need the records out
now and `close()` on shutdown (flush + stop; idempotent).

=== "TypeScript"

    ```ts
    import { Severity } from "@grow-codes/__KEY__";

    logs.send({ message: "payment accepted", severity: Severity.Info, attributes: { orderId: "o-42" } });
    logs.sendBatch([{ message: "a" }, { message: "b", severity: Severity.Warn }]);

    const log = logs.logger("checkout", { region: "eu" });   // facade, minSeverity Info
    log.info("cart created", { items: 3 });
    log.child({ userId: "u-1" }).error("card declined", { code: "05" });

    await logs.flush();
    console.log(logs.stats()); // { queued, sent, dropped, failed, retries }
    await logs.close();
    ```

=== "Rust"

    ```rust
    use grow___KEY_SNAKE__::logging::{LogClient, LogInput, Severity};
    use grow___KEY_SNAKE__::attrs;

    logs.send(LogInput::new("payment accepted").attribute("orderId", "o-42").into());
    logs.send_batch(vec!["a".into(), LogInput::new("b").severity(Severity::Warn).into()]);

    let log = logs.logger(Some("checkout"), attrs! { "region" => "eu" });
    log.info("cart created", attrs! { "items" => 3 });

    logs.flush(None).await?;
    println!("{:?}", logs.stats());
    logs.close().await?;
    ```

=== "Go"

    ```go
    logs.Send(ctx, __PKG__.LogInput{
        Message:    "payment accepted",
        Severity:   __PKG__.SeverityInfo,
        Attributes: map[string]__PKG__.AttrValue{"orderId": "o-42"},
    })
    logs.SendBatch(ctx, __PKG__.Entries(
        __PKG__.LogInput{Message: "a"},
        __PKG__.LogInput{Message: "b", Severity: __PKG__.SeverityWarn},
    ))

    log := logs.Logger("checkout", map[string]__PKG__.AttrValue{"region": "eu"})
    log.Info(ctx, "cart created", "items", 3) // slog-style key/value pairs

    if err := logs.Flush(ctx); err != nil {
        return err
    }
    fmt.Printf("%+v\n", logs.Stats())
    _ = logs.Close(ctx)
    ```

=== "Python"

    ```python
    from grow___KEY_SNAKE__ import LogInput, Severity

    logs.send(LogInput("payment accepted", attributes={"orderId": "o-42"}))
    logs.send_batch([LogInput("a"), LogInput("b", severity=Severity.WARN)])

    log = logs.logger("checkout", {"region": "eu"})
    log.info("cart created", {"items": 3})
    log.child({"userId": "u-1"}).error("card declined", {"code": "05"})

    logs.flush()
    print(logs.stats())
    logs.close()
    ```

    `AsyncBatchingLogClient` offers the same API with `await`.

=== "Java"

    ```java
    logs.send(LogInput.builder("payment accepted").attribute("orderId", "o-42").build());
    logs.sendBatch(List.of(
        LogInput.builder("a").build(),
        LogInput.builder("b").severity(Severity.WARN).build()));

    Logger log = logs.logger("checkout", Map.of("region", "eu"));
    log.info("cart created", Map.of("items", 3));

    logs.flush();
    System.out.println(logs.stats());
    logs.close();
    ```

## Batching

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| - | - | - |
| `maxQueueSize` | 2048 | records waiting in memory |
| `maxBatchSize` | 512 | records per export |
| `maxBatchBytes` | 1 MiB | UTF-8 JSON size per export |
| `flushInterval` | 1 s | export at least this often |
| `exportTimeout` | 30 s | deadline of one export |
| `dropPolicy` | `drop_newest` | when the queue is full: `drop_newest`, `drop_oldest` or `block` |
| `gzip` | `true` | compress exports |
| `onDrop(records, reason)` | — | `queue_full`, `shutdown` or `export_failed` |
| `onError(error, records)` | — | export errors (after retries) |

`add`/`send` never block unless `dropPolicy` is `block`. After `close()`, new records are dropped
with reason `shutdown`. `stats()` reports `queued, sent, dropped, failed, retries`.

## Redaction

Every record passes a `RedactionProcessor` before it is queued. Attribute **keys** that contain one
of the default keys (case-insensitive, recursive) get the value `[REDACTED]`:
`password`, `passwd`, `token`, `authorization`, `secret`, `cookie`, `api_key`, `apikey`,
`access_key`, `private_key`. Add your own keys and regular expressions (applied to the body and
string attribute values):

=== "TypeScript"

    ```ts
    import { DEFAULT_REDACT_KEYS, RedactionProcessor } from "@grow-codes/__KEY__";

    const redaction = new RedactionProcessor({
      keys: [...DEFAULT_REDACT_KEYS, "iban"],
      patterns: [/\b\d{16}\b/g],
    });
    ```

=== "Rust"

    ```rust
    use grow___KEY_SNAKE__::logging::{RedactionProcessor, DEFAULT_REDACT_KEYS};

    let keys = DEFAULT_REDACT_KEYS.iter().copied().chain(["iban"]);
    let redaction = RedactionProcessor::new(keys, vec![regex::Regex::new(r"\b\d{16}\b")?]);
    ```

=== "Go"

    ```go
    redaction := __PKG__.NewRedactionProcessor(__PKG__.RedactionOptions{
        Keys:     append(slices.Clone(__PKG__.DefaultRedactKeys), "iban"),
        Patterns: []*regexp.Regexp{regexp.MustCompile(`\b\d{16}\b`)},
    })
    ```

=== "Python"

    ```python
    import re
    from grow___KEY_SNAKE__ import DEFAULT_REDACT_KEYS, RedactionProcessor

    redaction = RedactionProcessor(keys=[*DEFAULT_REDACT_KEYS, "iban"], patterns=[re.compile(r"\b\d{16}\b")])
    ```

=== "Java"

    ```java
    RedactionProcessor redaction = RedactionProcessor.builder()
        .addKeys("iban")
        .pattern(Pattern.compile("\\b\\d{16}\\b"))
        .build();
    ```

## Framework adapters

Send the logs of your existing logging framework through the log client:

| Language | Adapter |
| - | - |
| TypeScript | pino: `pino(createPinoTransport(logs))`; winston: `new WinstonTransport(logs)` |
| Rust | `tracing_subscriber::registry().with(LogLayer::new(logs))` (feature `tracing-layer`); `LogBridge::new(logs).init()` for the `log` crate (feature `log-bridge`) |
| Go | `slog.New(__PKG__.NewSlogHandler(logs, nil))`; zap: `zapadapter.NewLogger(logs, zapadapter.Options{})` |
| Python | `logging.getLogger().addHandler(LogHandler(logs))`; structlog: `structlog_processor(logs)` |
| Java | Logback `GrowLogbackAppender.install(context, logs)`, Log4j2 `GrowLog4j2Appender`, `java.util.logging` `GrowJulHandler` |

When an OpenTelemetry span is active and the record has no trace id, `traceId`, `spanId` and
`traceFlags` come from the active span, so logs and traces correlate.

## Search logs

`LogQueryClient` is available when __DISPLAY__ has a query API (otherwise its methods raise
`UNSUPPORTED`; see [Compatibility](compatibility.md)).

| Function | Returns | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| `search(query, opts?)` | `LogSearchResult { records, nextCursor?, total? }` | `opts`: `start`, `end`, `limit` (100), `order` (`desc`/`asc`), `cursor` |
| `tail(query, onRecord, opts?)` | `TailHandle` (`stop()`) | streams or polls; `UNSUPPORTED` when the service can do neither |
| `listStreams()` / `listLabels()` | names | |
| `waitForLog(query, opts?)` | `LogRecord` | polls `search` until a record matches; `TIMEOUT` after `timeout` (30 s) |

=== "TypeScript"

    ```ts
    const result = await query.search("orderId:o-42", { limit: 20, start: new Date(Date.now() - 3600_000) });
    for (const r of result.records) console.log(r.timestamp, r.severityText, r.body);
    const record = await query.waitForLog("payment accepted", { timeoutMs: 10_000 });
    ```

=== "Rust"

    ```rust
    let result = query.search("orderId:o-42", SearchOptions { limit: Some(20), ..Default::default() }).await?;
    for r in &result.records {
        println!("{:?} {} {}", r.timestamp, r.severity_text, r.body);
    }
    ```

=== "Go"

    ```go
    result, err := query.Search(ctx, "orderId:o-42", __PKG__.SearchOptions{Limit: 20})
    for _, r := range result.Records {
        fmt.Println(r.Timestamp, r.SeverityText, r.Body)
    }
    record, err := query.WaitForLog(ctx, "payment accepted", __PKG__.WaitForLogOptions{Timeout: 10 * time.Second})
    ```

=== "Python"

    ```python
    result = query.search("orderId:o-42", limit=20)
    for r in result.records:
        print(r.timestamp, r.severity_text, r.body)
    record = query.wait_for_log("payment accepted", timeout_s=10.0)
    ```

=== "Java"

    ```java
    LogSearchResult result = query.search("orderId:o-42", SearchOptions.builder().limit(20).build());
    result.records().forEach(r -> System.out.println(r.timestamp() + " " + r.body()));
    LogRecord record = query.waitForLog("payment accepted",
        WaitForLogOptions.builder().timeout(Duration.ofSeconds(10)).build());
    ```

## Testing

The testing module has an in-memory log client and query client (see
[Docker testing](docker-testing.md#test-fakes-for-your-own-tests)).
